title: Progenitor transcriptional alterations link fetal and adult pathology in Huntington’s disease
title_zh: 祖细胞转录改变连接亨廷顿病的胎儿期与成人期病理
abstract: Abstract Huntington’s disease (HD) is an autosomal dominant neurodegenerative disorder caused by a CAG repeat expansion in the HTT gene. Although the mutant huntingtin protein is expressed from conception, clinical symptoms typically emerge in mid-adulthood. Imaging and molecular studies have raised the possibility that HD may involve neurodevelopmental abnormalities, but direct evidence at the single-cell level in the human fetal brain has been lacking. Here we investigated whether early, cell type–specific transcriptional vulnerabilities arise during neurodevelopment, persist into adult pathology, and might be rescued. To address this, we performed single-cell transcriptomic profiling of the lateral ganglionic eminence (LGE) and cortex from a rare, anatomically intact human HD fetal brain, alongside matched controls. These data were complemented by an allelic series of HD mouse embryos and cross-compared with already published human post-mortem brains and brain organoid models’ datasets. Neural progenitors displayed the highest number of differentially expressed genes in the human fetal brain, and were also impacted in the HD mouse model, where additional cell types displayed transcriptional alterations. Notably, human HD progenitor transcriptional signatures were moderately enriched in the developing mouse LGE. These progenitors exhibited increased expression of synaptic pathways coupled with reduced expression of cell maintenance genes. Cross-comparison with publicly available post-mortem HD datasets revealed that components of this transcriptional signature persist into adulthood. Furthermore, cellular interactions were found to mitigate these alterations, highlighting a potentially rescuable fetal-to-adult transcriptional signature with important implications for HD pathogenesis and therapeutic strategies. Together, these findings reinforce the view of HD as a disorder with developmental origins, in which early transcriptional changes may shape neuronal function while increasing susceptibility to later neurodegeneration.
abstract_zh: 摘要 亨廷顿病（HD）是一种常染色体显性遗传的神经退行性疾病，由 HTT 基因中的 CAG 重复扩增引起。尽管突变的亨廷顿蛋白从受精开始就表达，但临床症状通常在中年期出现。影像学和分子研究提示 HD 可能涉及神经发育异常，但在人类胎儿大脑中缺乏单细胞水平的直接证据。我们在此研究了在神经发育过程中是否出现早期、细胞类型特异性的转录易感性，并在成人病理中持续存在，且是否可被修复。为此，我们对一例罕见、解剖完整的 HD 胎儿大脑的侧神经节前叶（LGE）和皮层进行单细胞转录组测序，并与匹配的对照组进行比较。随后将这些数据与 HD 小鼠胚胎的等位基因系列以及已发表的人类尸检脑和脑类器官模型的数据进行交叉比较。神经祖细胞在人体胎儿脑中表现出最高数量的差异表达基因，并且在 HD 小鼠模型中也受到影响，其他细胞类型也出现转录改变。值得注意的是，人类 HD 祖细胞的转录特征在发育中的小鼠 LGE 中中度富集。这些祖细胞表现出突触通路表达上调、细胞维持基因表达下调。与公开可获得的尸检 HD 数据集进行交叉比较后发现，该转录特征的组成部分在成年期仍然存在。进一步的细胞相互作用研究表明，这些改变可以被缓解，提示存在一种可被修复的胎儿到成人的转录特征，对 HD 病理和治疗策略具有重要意义。综上所述，这些发现进一步支持 HD 是一种具有发育起源的疾病，早期转录改变可能塑造神经元功能并增加后期神经退行性变的易感性。
